items.declaration: object Product4.unapply[T1, T2, T3, T4](x: Product4[T1, T2, T3, T4]): Option[Product4[T1, T2, T3, T4]]
items.comment: Accurate: `unapply` always returns `Some(x)`, and wrapping the whole product (rather than a tuple) is exactly what lets any `Product4` implementor be destructured via `case Product4(a, b, c, d) => ...`, matching the 'usable as an extractor' claim. First sentence is a good standalone summary, third person, present tense. Minor style point: the first sentence already begins with 'Returns the given product wrapped in a [[scala.Some]]...' which fully states the return value, so per the @return-drop convention the `@return` tag ('the product `x` wrapped in a [[scala.Some]]') is redundant and could be omitted. Not blocking.
